premortem.failure_story: We buy USD/JPY right below 160, and Japanese Ministry of Finance officials immediately announce a joint intervention with the US Treasury. The pair suffers a sudden 200-pip drop, triggering our stop loss instantly.

decision.reason: Intervention risk by Japanese authorities near the 160 round-number level creates an unfavorable risk-reward profile for taking long positions right below resistance, despite overall positive momentum.
decision.odds_reasoning: Passing due to prohibitive intervention risk at the 160 barrier overriding standard technical momentum signals.
decision.thesis: While the interest rate gap favors the US dollar, buying right under 160 invites direct intervention from Japanese authorities. The desk's base rate for short/fade is poor (-0.87 R average), and entering longs into an official ceiling violates prudent risk management. Therefore, passing is the disciplined choice.
decision.invalidation: An official pullback toward the 20-day average near 158.23 without intervention action would re-open long setups.
decision.plain_english: We are passing on trading USD/JPY [US Dollar to Japanese Yen exchange rate] because the price is right below 160, where Japanese officials have threatened to intervene and crash the currency. Buying here has a terrible risk-reward profile because government intervention could wipe out profits instantly. It is better to stay in cash than fight a central bank at a key round-number resistance level.
